payload.statement_nl:
Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-a q^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d. Then there exists a nonnegative integer B such that for every integer n > 1 satisfying n ≡ 1 mod 2d there exists a Laurent polynomial in X over Z[q^±1] of the form C_{d,r,n}(X,q) = ∑_{j=-B}^{B} c_j(q) X^j, with each c_j(q) in Z[q^±1], having the following property. Define the modulus M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n define
T_{d,r,n,k}(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k,
and define
G_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q) · C_{d,r,n}(q^k,q).
Also define
H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2},
and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 define
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q).
Then H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for every integer k with 0 <= k <= n-1, and there exist polynomials A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1, gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1, G_{d,r,n,0}(q) = M_n(q) A_0(q) / B_0(q), and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) = M_n(q) A_n(q) / B_n(q).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: I followed the requested decomposition on the disproof path: (1) I derived the explicit ratio R_{1,1,n,k}(q)=T_{k+1}(q)/T_k(q); (2) I rewrote the telescoping condition as the recurrence C_n(q^k,q)-R_k(q)C_n(q^{k+1},q)=1 for 1<=k<=n-1; (3) instead of asserting generic nonexistence, I used the bounded support hypothesis to build an explicit Laurent polynomial P_n(X,q) with support independent of n except through B, then chose n=2B+13 so that P_n has more roots than its degree allows, forcing a functional identity; (4) I then proved that functional identity has no Laurent-polynomial solution by separate lowest- and highest-exponent arguments. The endpoint divisibility conditions are therefore moot, because the telescoping identities already cannot be satisfied.
result_payload.candidate_counterexample: Parametric counterexample family: fix d = r = 1. For any proposed uniform support bound B, take the admissible odd integer n = 2B + 13. Then no Laurent polynomial C_{1,1,n}(X,q) supported in X-exponents [-B,B] can satisfy the required telescoping identities for k = 1,...,n-1.

counterexample_flag.reason: For d = r = 1, bounded-support telescoping would force a Laurent-polynomial functional identity D(X,q)(C(X,q)-1)=N(X,q)C(qX,q). A root-counting argument shows this identity must hold whenever n is large relative to the support bound B, and a lowest-/highest-exponent comparison shows that no Laurent polynomial C can satisfy it. Hence no uniform B can exist.

result_payload.proof_summary:
I believe the lemma is false.

Fix d = r = 1. Assume a uniform bound B exists. For any admissible odd n and any proposed witness C_n(X,q) = sum_{j=-B}^B c_j(q) X^j, the required identities for 1 <= k <= n-1 give

C_n(q^k,q) - R_k(q) C_n(q^{k+1},q) = 1,

with explicit ratio

R_k(q) = q^{-k-1} * (1-q^{3k+4})/(1-q^{3k+1}) * (1-q^{2k+1})^3 * (1-q^{k+1})/(1+q^{k+1}).

Equivalently, if

R(X,q) = q^{-1} X^{-1} (1-q^4 X^3)(1-q X^2)^3(1-qX) / ((1-qX^3)(1+qX)),
D(X,q) = (1-qX^3)(1+qX),
N(X,q) = q^{-1} X^{-1}(1-q^4 X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX),

then

P_n(X,q) := D(X,q)(C_n(X,q)-1) - N(X,q) C_n(qX,q)

satisfies P_n(q^k,q)=0 for k=1,...,n-1.

Because C_n has X-support in [-B,B], P_n has X-support in [-(B+1), B+9]. So X^{B+1} P_n is a polynomial in X of degree at most 2B+10 over Q(q). Taking n = 2B+13 (which is admissible), this polynomial has 2B+12 distinct roots X = q, q^2, ..., q^{2B+12}. Hence it must be the zero polynomial, so P_n(X,q)=0 identically.

Thus any such C_n would satisfy

D(X,q)(C_n(X,q)-1) = N(X,q) C_n(qX,q).

But no Laurent polynomial can satisfy this: if m is its minimal X-exponent and m<0, the left side has minimal exponent m while the right side has minimal exponent m-1; contradiction. Hence m>=0, so C_n is an ordinary polynomial of degree M. Then the left side has degree at most M+4, while the right side has degree exactly M+9 because N has leading term -q^7 X^9; contradiction.

Therefore for every proposed B, choosing d=r=1 and n=2B+13 gives a failure. So the lemma's uniform bounded-support certificate statement cannot be true.
